findings.area: names.ts LOWER table vs prepare() (NFKC runs first)
findings.title: The Greek lunate sigma (U+03F9 capital, U+03F2 small), drawn exactly like a Latin C, is documented as folded to 'c' but never is: NFKC turns it into Sigma / final sigma before the table is applied, so 'Dr. <U+03F9>laire Moreau' registers as a teacher next to (and as a twin of) the reserved demo teacher
findings.evidence: names.ts:31-32 lists 'ϲ: c' in LOWER (and KNOWN_LIMITATIONS round 10/11 say lunate sigma is folded), but prepare() starts with v.normalize('NFKC'), and NFKC(U+03F2) = U+03C2 (final sigma) and NFKC(U+03F9) = U+03A3 (Sigma); foldCase then makes both sigma. The table entry is dead code (scan: of all LOWER keys only 'ϲ' does not survive NFKC + case fold with itself). nameKey('Claire')='ciaire' but nameKey('\u03F9laire')='\u03C3iaire'. Live on a NODE_ENV=test server: POST /api/auth/register teacherInviteCode ok name 'Dr. Ϲlaire Moreau' -> 201 (Cyrillic С, fullwidth Ｃ, roman Ⅽ, Greek α variants of the same name are all 409 name_taken). The same dead entry also lets a lunate-sigma spelling of the correct option label pass the AI-hint label guard (skeleton() is shared). Not a round-14 regression (older), found while scanning code points for key changes.
findings.repro: scratchpad/r15-A/t_lunate.mjs (BASE=http://127.0.0.1:5903 node --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning t_lunate.mjs; needs a server with a high RATE_REGISTER_PER_HOUR and TEACHER_INVITE_CODE=R15-INVITE); key level: scratchpad/r15-A/lun.ts
findings.expected: 'Dr. Ϲlaire Moreau' (and any name with U+03F2 / U+03F9 in place of C / c) has the same key as the Latin spelling: 409 name_taken, reserved demo name stays reserved.
findings.actual: 201 Created; a visually identical teacher name is accepted (review records stay distinguishable only through '(teacher #id)').
findings.fix_hint: be/src/names.ts prepare()/skeleton()/classNameKey(): replace U+03F2 and U+03F9 by 'c' BEFORE the first NFKC (e.g. v.replace(/[\u03F2\u03F9]/gu,'c').normalize('NFKC')), or drop the dead entry and document it. Add a test that every LOWER key survives prepare() unchanged (the same scan found no other dead key).

findings.title: The R14-A-01 fix drops a stray U+0345 everywhere except after alpha / eta / omega, where NFKC composes it into an iota-subscript letter whose key reads 'ai' / 'hi' / 'wi': a Greek teacher name plus one U+0345 is still a different key, so a visually near-identical twin of any Greek name containing alpha, eta or omega is accepted
findings.evidence: Live (server on 5901, then the same on a fresh DB): register 'Μαρία Παπαδοπούλου' -> 201; 'Μαρία Παπαδοπούλου' again -> 409; 'Μαρίᾳ Παπαδοπούλου' (alpha + U+0345 or precomposed ᾳ) -> 201 (key 'μαριαι...' vs 'μαρια...'); 'Μαρία\u0345 Παπαδοπούλου' then 409 only because it equals the twin just created. Same for 'Ελένη Κωνσταντίνου' then 'Ελένῃ Κωνσταντίνου' -> 201, 201. The R14 test (r14-fixes.test.ts:52-80) appends marks to a LATIN name and to bases whose last letter is Greek only with other marks; the documentation says a U+0345 after α/η/ω 'stays equivalent to αι' and does not mention that this is a twin route. Case-folding forces ᾳ = ΑΙ (toUpperCase('ᾳ') = 'ΑΙ'), so one key cannot both keep the diphthong 'αι' distinct from 'α' and ignore the subscript.
findings.repro: scratchpad/r15-A/t_names_api.mjs (node --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning t_names_api.mjs against any server with TEACHER_INVITE_CODE=R15-INVITE); key level: scratchpad/r15-A/names1.ts prints 'name:append:Ωραία 1 U+345', 'name:append:Ἀθηνᾶ 1 U+345'
findings.expected: A single U+0345 added to a name is never enough to make a new teacher name (as for Latin names, where the scan over all code points finds no exception).
findings.actual: For Greek names that contain α, η or ω the mark becomes the letter ι in the key and the twin is accepted (201).
findings.fix_hint: be/src/names.ts prepare(): decide explicitly. Either (a) map the iota-subscript letters (ᾀ-ᾯ, ᾳ ῃ ῳ and their capitals) to the plain letter before foldCase, accepting that ᾳ != ΑΙ, so a subscript is an accent like any other; or (b) keep the current behaviour and document it in KNOWN_LIMITATIONS as an accepted twin route for Greek names (the rest of the doc already lists residual lookalikes). Add a test with 'Μαρία' / 'Ελένη'.

findings.category: answer leak (AI hint guard, only with LAB_ASSISTANT_* configured)
findings.title: The positional guard is a closed list of phrasings: bare or lightly decorated option letters, spaced letters, Roman numerals, bare numbers and many natural 'pointing' verbs still name the correct option and are delivered as a paid assistant hint ('C'est C', which the code comment claims, is not caught either)
findings.evidence: leaksAnswer(text, hem-03-s2) (correct option C, 'Iron deficiency anemia') returns false for: "C'est C", "c'est C", '**C**', 'C)', 'C.', 'C:', '“C”', '«C»', '<C>', '__C__', 'Look at C', 'Consider C', 'I would say C', 'Focus on C', 'Hint: C', 'Think C!', 'Tick/Mark/Circle/Check/Click/Tap/Press C', 'C is the one', 'C is not wrong', 'C, definitely', 'O p t i o n C' (spaced letters), 'A n s w e r : C', 'C i s c o r r e c t', 'OptionC', 'AnswerC', 'Option III', 'option iii', 'Option Ⅲ', 'Option Ϲ' (lunate, see R15-A-01), 'Choose 3', 'Go with 3', 'Pick 3', 'It is 3', 'No. 3', '#3', '3)', 'Go with the last' / 'Choose the last' for the last option; for D: 'D.', 'I would say D', 'Focus on D'. 94 of 204 templates x 4 option positions were missed in the first sweep (many are letter-A false negatives by design because of the article 'a'; the B/C/D misses above are real). Delivered end to end through Game with a stub provider: guarded phrases fall back to source 'standard' with the faculty text, hint_log.text == response == hintsGiven, penalty -15 (arithmetic fine); the unguarded ones are delivered as source 'assistant'. False positives are negligible (vitamin C, C-reactive protein, hepatitis B/C, group B, 'Option' alone, hints about other options, units, 'step 3', '37 °C', clinical values all pass; all 77 faculty hints / rechecks / prompts / contexts of choice and decision steps pass; only the contrived 'Option 1 of the form...' is dropped on A steps). The provider request body is fine: options listed by position (letters A-D), default decisions included, no marking of the correct one.
findings.repro: scratchpad/r15-A/leak4.ts (135 phrasings for option C), scratchpad/r15-A/leak1.ts (204 templates x 4 positions), scratchpad/r15-A/leak2.ts (misses + false-positive + faculty-text pass), scratchpad/r15-A/hint_e2e.ts (end to end with stub provider)
findings.expected: A hint whose only content about the options is the correct option's letter, number or position is dropped; the code comment (assistant.ts, 'C'est C') is true.
findings.actual: Bare letters/numbers, spaced letters, Roman numerals and ~35 further natural phrasings pass the guard and reach the learner for the hint price. Documented as 'a last line of defence', but the documentation lists only the caught phrases, not these.
findings.fix_hint: assistant.ts:150-190 namesOptionByPosition: (1) treat a capital option letter that stands alone as a token (not part of a hyphenated or lettered term such as Vitamin C / C-reactive / hepatitis C / group B, not 'A' at sentence start) in a hint as a leak, because the fallback hint costs the same; (2) tokenise single-letter runs ('O p t i o n') before matching; (3) add Roman numerals and the CHOOSING verbs to the number branch; (4) fix the elision handling so "C'est C" reaches the PRONOUN test (tokenize() drops 'c'' so 'est' has no pronoun before it). Also give the system prompt a stronger 'never write a letter or number' line (assistant.ts:231 already asks).

findings.title: HEAD is not safe: a HEAD on GET /api/attempts/:id (or /result, /dashboard ...) runs the same expireStale() write as GET and flips an overdue attempt to 'expired'
findings.evidence: Harness with a controllable clock: start hem-01, advance 3 h, HEAD /api/attempts/:id -> 200 and attempts.status changed from in_progress to expired (game.ts:251-297 expireStale on a read path). Everything else about HEAD held: 96 GET/HEAD pairs over all GET routes x anon / student / teacher / forged token (+ unknown routes, bad percent-encoding, 3000-char query) have identical status and headers, empty body and Content-Length equal to the GET body; anon -> 401, student on teacher route -> 403; HEAD on a path with no GET route -> 405 with Allow lacking GET/HEAD; Allow on a 405 for GET+PUT paths = 'GET, HEAD, PUT, OPTIONS'; HEAD /api/openapi.json 200 with Content-Length 26165; HEAD with a body and pipelined GET on the same socket stays in sync; no rate-limiter hit on HEAD; CORS headers identical.
findings.expected: A HEAD never changes server state.
findings.actual: The expiry is time-determined and would be materialised by the next GET, so no data is wrong; it is a safe-method violation inherited from GET.
findings.fix_hint: app.ts:140: pass a flag (ctx.safe = req.method === 'HEAD') and let expireStale skip the write on HEAD, or document that GET on attempts materialises expiry.

findings.title: The start-up write probe turns a write lock held by another process for more than the 5 s busy timeout into a fatal 'database is locked' on a healthy database that used to start; and two read-only cases still show a raw SQLite sentence instead of the friendly one
findings.evidence: (a) Another process holds BEGIN IMMEDIATE for 7.5 s: openDb on the healthy copy fails after 5.2 s with 'database is locked' (server.ts prints 'cannot use the database at <path>: database is locked', exit 1); the same file opened with the probe removed starts in 4 ms. (b) The friendly sentence 'the database file is not writable (read-only permissions or file system) ...' only appears when the failure happens on PRAGMA user_version: a rollback-journal (non-WAL) database with mode 0444 fails earlier on PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL, and a writable main file whose -wal/-shm sidecars are 0444 fails on BEGIN IMMEDIATE (db.ts:314, outside the try); both end start-up with one line ending in the raw 'attempt to write a readonly database'. Held: probe never commits (file sha1 and mtime identical across opens, WAL mode unchanged, no lock left behind: sqlite3 can write while the probe's process is still alive), newer schema (v99) is refused before any change (sha1 identical, also at 0444), v0 / v5 / v6 databases migrate to v7 with integrity ok, 12 processes x 100 rounds starting at once on a healthy DB: 1200/1200 OK (<= 41 ms) also while 8 writers hammer the server (0 5xx), db:check works on a 0444 file. Root-run semantics could not be run (uid 501).
findings.repro: scratchpad/r15-A/open2.ts + open2old.ts (probe removed), scratchpad/r15-A/loop2.sh, the lock/readonly commands are in the session log
findings.expected: A short lock held by a peer is waited out (it is); a long one is reported as 'another process holds the database' or does not block a start that needs no write; every read-only cause gets the same friendly line.
findings.fix_hint: db.ts:309-322: wrap BEGIN IMMEDIATE in the same try, map /readonly/i for it, and skip the probe (or only warn) on SQLITE_BUSY after the timeout; journal_mode failure (db.ts:337) could be mapped to the same message.

findings.title: namesOptionByPosition is quadratic: a 1 MB text of repeated 'C ' takes 125 s of event-loop time; unreachable today only because both callers test the 400-character limit first
findings.evidence: perf1.ts on hem-03-s2: 'C C C ...' (1 MB) = 124,986 ms; other 1 MB inputs 0.4-1.3 s (option/the/is repeats, U+0345 pairs 1.1 s, sigma 1.3 s); hasSubstance alone is linear (3-390 ms per MB). Cause: bracketed()/clauseEnd()/compound() slice and regex-scan the whole text per letter token (assistant.ts bracketed(), prefix slice + /[(\[{]\s*$/). In Game.cleanAssistantHint and AnthropicHintProvider the order is hasSubstance || exceedsHintLimit || leaksAnswer, so leaksAnswer only ever sees <= 400 code points; the provider response itself is not size-capped before hasSubstance (res.json() of an arbitrarily large body).
findings.expected: Linear time in the text length, or a length check before any work.
findings.actual: Latent quadratic; becomes a freeze if leaksAnswer is ever called before the length check or exported use grows.
findings.fix_hint: Check exceedsHintLimit (and a byte cap on the provider body) before hasSubstance; make bracketed() look at a 3-character window around the token.

findings.title: A password of ten invisible characters (ZWSP, U+3164, U+2800) is accepted, and the schema's minLength still counts code points before NFC so '5 x U+0344' (10 characters after NFC) is refused with a message that says the count is made after NFC
findings.evidence: POST /api/auth/register with password U+200B x10 and U+3164 x10 -> 201; with U+0344 x5 and U+0958 x6 -> 400 'body.password must be at least 10 characters' (schema, raw count) although NFC gives 10 / 12. Held: 9 chars 400, 10 chars 201, e+U+0301 x5 400 (policy message, NFC count), x10 201, whitespace-only (spaces, NBSP, U+3000) 400, NUL / tab / newline 400, 200 chars ok, 201 chars 400, 200 astral ok, 200 x U+0344 (NFC 400 chars) ok, lone surrogates ok; policy 400s do not consume the registration budget (3/h server: 3 x 201 then 429, short and blank passwords still 400 after the limit); the 400 is identical for a taken and a free e-mail (no enumeration); NFC and NFD logins both work for an NFC and an NFD registration; legacy hashes (3-char password, whitespace password, raw-NFD hash) still log in (a raw-NFD hash needs the NFD form, as documented); demo accounts and POST /auth/demo unaffected.
findings.expected: Invisible-only secrets treated like whitespace-only; the schema and the handler count the same way.
findings.actual: Cosmetic: weak but valid secrets and an inconsistent count in two exotic cases.
findings.fix_hint: routes.ts:99 use the same invisible-character test as hasVisibleCharacter(); drop minLength from the register schema (or document 'raw count at least 10 and NFC count at least 10').

notes: Environment: node v22.23.2; own servers 5901 (NODE_ENV unset, DEMO, register limit 1000/h), 5902 (low limits, CORS pinned), 5903 (NODE_ENV=test, DEMO); all on throwaway DBs under scratchpad/r15-A, all three stopped by pid file at the end; nothing under be/ web/ docs/ sources/ edited, be/data untouched, be/openapi.json not regenerated in place (generated to scratchpad/r15-A/openapi.gen.json: byte-identical; docs/SCIENTIFIC_REVIEW_BACKLOG.md changed during my run but not by me). Baseline: cd be && npm test = 223/223 pass, tsc --noEmit clean. HELD (could not break): (1) names: exhaustive scan of all 1,114,112 code points appended / prepended / inserted / after a space on 9 base names (Latin, Greek polytonic with iota subscript, Δάιος, Ηλιάδης, Ωραία, Cyrillic): only U+0345 after a Greek alpha/eta/omega (R15-A-02) and the real Cyrillic letters formed by a breve / diaeresis / U+0344 on a Cyrillic base (ӑ ӓ, by design, not a stray mark) change the key; every code point plus 600k pair and 4-letter Greek strings keep the key under NFC/NFD/NFKC/NFKD and upper/lower case (class key too); sigma spacing independence holds; because the key is one function, transitivity across rename chains cannot fail (rename path app: game.ts:784 compares keys). 'αι' as a diaeresis-free diphthong in Δάιος / Ωραία / Ηλιάδης does not collide with a different name (live: 'Ωραία Δάιος', 'Ηλιάδης Δάιος' both 201; the same name with Δάϊος 409). Dead table entry found: only ϲ (R15-A-01). (2) database: see R15-A-05; 25 x 12 and 100 x 12 process races on a FRESH file show 'database is locked' in about 0.25% of starts both with and without the probe (journal_mode switch race, db.ts:337, pre-existing, not caused by round 14). (3) hints: 135 + 204x4 phrasings, 33 false-positive probes x 12 steps, 77 faculty texts, 12 end-to-end stub-provider cases (leak, null, throw, blank, 401 chars, 400 emoji): no false positive worth reporting, source 'standard' fallback and penalty -15 correct. (4) generic: route x token x body x id matrix 3,912 cells vs openapi: 0 undeclared statuses, 0 5xx; 3,000-request random fuzz (methods incl. HEAD / TRACE, hostile paths, headers, bodies, U+0345, lone surrogates): 0 5xx, 0 stack traces in the server log; answer-leak scan (2 players x all 10 missions, all six engines, start / get / wrong / hint / get-after / right / result, 151 responses): 0 leaks of explanation, unbought hint, recheck before earning or key fields; state machine: 12 parallel correct answers = one 200 + eleven 409, 12 parallel wrong = 12 counted, 6 parallel hints = 2 delivered (rest 409 no_more_hints / in progress), IDOR on GET / answer / hint / result of another player's attempt = 404, future step 409, answer after completion 409, result stable; kill -9 during 8-writer registration load then db:check = problems [] and restart healthy.
